newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shun Tak says ferry passengers grow.
newsitem.headline: Shun Tak says ferry passengers grow.

text.p: Shun Tak Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday passengers on its high-speed ferries between Hong Kong and Macau rose some two percent in the past six months in line with overall market growth.

"We have seen that in the past six months, there was already already a growth of two percent in the number of passengers going to Macau...There was negative growth for one and a half years and now at last it is starting to grow again," chairman Stanley Ho told reporters.
The chairman added passengers carried by the company's fleet, which accounts for about 75 percent of the Hong Kong-Macau traffic, had posted growth similar to that of the overall market.
Director Pansy Ho said the Hong Kong-Macau traffic market had grown between two and three percent since the end of June.
She said she was optimistic about market growth next year.
The chairman said he expected the company's shipping business to be stable in 1997 and continue to account for some 70 percent of total group revenues.
